title: Evangelicals Don't Produce Leaders. They Produce Cubicle Men.
author: Aaron Renn
summary: Renn argues that evangelical Christian culture, despite its emphasis on leadership development and biblical authority, actually produces men trained for compliance and middle management rather than genuine leadership. The church's emphasis on deference to authority, avoidance of conflict, and maintenance of institutional peace creates men who excel at following others' visions but struggle to articulate and pursue their own. Renn contends that true leadership requires courage, conviction, and willingness to challenge existing structures—qualities that evangelical culture often discourages in favor of harmony and obedience. The result is a generation of capable men constrained by institutional timidity, unable to think independently or take decisive action. Renn calls for a reimagining of male formation in evangelical contexts that prioritizes character and conviction over compliance.
points: Evangelical Christian culture produces men trained for compliance and middle management rather than genuine leadership despite emphasis on biblical authority.
